detail:
Full summary: Review finding on fix/repo-ids CONFIRMED, not refuted: a store that ran identity init and was then migrated by a pre-591fcf63 `migrate --to 3` keeps the path-seeded store_id/repo_id on every rerun (resolveIdentity returns legacy/migration-state.json's identity first; finalize can only union ids the CURRENT store.json declares, and the init ids were overwritten out of it). Reproduced on the fixed code by moving the init descriptor aside for the first run (the seed is the store path, so the pair is the one the old code minted) and pinned as a test in test/migrate/v3-identity-reuse.test.ts. No heal path added — the reviewer's own fix says none is required for this commit and the heal is a design choice (see decisions). Applied the exact detection the reviewer asked for: `twining doctor` now reports bindings.repo_ids_cited (every scope.repo the journal cites), bindings.repo_ids_undeclared (cited but absent from store.json repo_ids) and an honest_limits line naming the ids when the set is non-empty; two doctor cases added in test/cli/v3-verbs.test.ts. resolveIdentity's doc comment names the limitation. Tests: v3-identity-reuse 5/5, v3-verbs 27/27, tsc clean.
Decisions: Chose NOT to add a migrate heal path for stores migrated pre-591fcf63 after identity init — the events minted before that migration cite the init repo id and the ~45 migration events cite the seeded one, both immutable, so healing means choosing which id the checkout cites from now on (and whether repo_ids[0] flips, which changes what every new event cites); that is an operator decision to make once and deliberately, not one a rerun may make on its own. Alternatives weighed: (a) resolveIdentity preferring the descriptor over prior.identity — breaks rerun idempotency for every normal store; (b) finalize unioning repo ids cited by events into repo_ids — silently legitimises a split-brain store and still has to pick a primary. Would be invalidated by: a ruling that the init ids always win, at which point a `twining doctor --heal`/migrate flag can implement that rule against this pinned test.; Chose to put the detection in `twining doctor` (repo_ids_cited / repo_ids_undeclared in bindings + an honest_limits line) over migrateStatus — doctor already opens the runtime and fetches journalRows(), which carry scope per row, so the check is ~10 read-only lines with no new failure mode, whereas migrateStatus is a cheap tool-loop read that only counts files and would have to parse every event.; Chose the exact check (repo ids the journal cites vs ids store.json declares) and did NOT encode the reviewer's heuristic (b), a migration-state store_id lacking the ULID timestamp prefix — it is an id-shape heuristic (a path-seeded derivedId starts with 01M with probability ~1/1024) and it flags stores where nothing ever cited the init id, which are harmless; the exact check catches precisely the harmful case because the ceremony membership and every pre-migration event are events that cite the init repo id.; Chose to pin the limitation as a permanent test that moves the identity-init descriptor aside for the first migrate run rather than checking out the old source — the seeded pair is a pure function of the store path, so the resulting store.json and migration-state.json are byte-for-byte the shape the pre-fix code left, and the test names what a future 'fix' that makes it fail would actually be deciding.; Chose branch fix/repo-ids-review (from 591fcf63, the fix/repo-ids tip) in this worktree rather than fix/repo-ids — that branch is checked out in worktree wf_7fdd8f5c-571-1, so git refuses a second checkout; the caller fast-forwards fix/repo-ids to the reported sha. The task's literal recipe (branch from fix/working-set-render) would have dropped the fix commit the finding is about, so it was read as a template and the fix tip used instead.
summary: Review finding on fix/repo-ids CONFIRMED, not refuted: a store that ran identity init and was then migrated by a pre-591fcf63 `migrate --to 3` keeps the path-seeded store_id/repo_id on every rerun …
